Output 1: Barriers to socio-economic (re)integration sustainably addressed
Indicator 1.1: Number of people on the move and host communities benefitting from integrated and targeted interventions, including on strengthening social cohesion (disaggregated by sex and status) (IRRF 3.4.2)
Sudan: 
Baseline: 2,000 HH/10,000 individuals (FW1)
Target: 5,211 HH/ 26,055 individuals
Related CPD outcomes:
Sudan: Conflict-affected livelihoods revitalized and stabilized (Output 2.1).
Gender Marker: GEN2 
Enhance access to community socio-economic infrastructure 
-	Emergency employment for 2000 people through Cash for Work for clearing irrigation canals and construction and rehabilitation of critical community infrastructure, ensuring women’s participation 
-	Provide socio-economic productive and critical infrastructure to vulnerable groups at the community level (e.g., vegetable gardens, greenhouses, bakeries, grinding mills, grain storage, markets, Solar equipment etc.) (target 60% women). 
-	Provide farm machinery to expand production including tractors and accessories to be managed by the CMC (target at least 50% women, empowering women through mechanization)

Output 2: Vulnerable women (IDP, host and returnees) have more resilient livelihoods and can start/sustain climate-smart businesses
Indicator 2.1: % of female MSME owners able to sustain their businesses in the first 6 months 
Sudan specific indicator 2.1: Number of government/civil society institutions with enhanced capacity to support gender-responsive solutions to internal displacement 
Baseline: 8 (FW 1) 
Target: 17

2.2 % of female MSMEs owners [groups and associations] able to sustain their businesses in the first 6 months 
Baseline: 0 
Target: 60% (10 out of 17) 

Related CPD outcomes: 
Sudan: Conflict-affected livelihoods revitalized and stabilized (Output 2.1)
Gender Marker: GEN 3
Restore productive and income-generation opportunities for IDPs and host communities;  
-	Establish and train Agriculture and Fisheries Associations 
-	Provide agriculture and fisheries inputs for gardening, winter crop production (including seeds, tools, solar water pumps, fishing gears, fertilizers and agrochemicals 
-	Facilitate access to land by landless households, including women-headed households 
-	Provide extension services to smallholder farmers (men and women) 
-	Conduct livestock restocking for the most vulnerable; focusing on small ruminants. 
-	Support local seed security through seed multiplication and seed banking for local varieties 
-	Establish/reactivate and register voluntary Saving Associations and capacitate them on organizational management while ensuring that at least 50% are women-led, focusing on women’s economic empowerment 
-	Provide micro-grants to groups and associations (including IDPs and host community members) to initiate joint activities such as bakeries, restaurants, grain mills, small businesses, petty trading, food processing while ensuring at least 50% of this groups are women-led or owns, focusing on women’s economic empowerment

Output 3: Local authorities have improved capacity to lead local solutions to address internal displacement  

Indicator 3.1. % of government officials demonstrating improved skills in designing solutions to internal displacement 
Indicator 3.2. Number of institutions that have mainstreamed human mobility into their development policies and plans (IRRF 3.4.1)
Sudan specific indicator 3.1: Percentage of women-led local institutions with the capacity to promote recovery
Baseline: 0
Target:  50%

Related CPD outcomes: 
Sudan: Conflict-affected livelihoods revitalized and stabilized (Output 2.1)
Gender Marker: GEN 2
Build the capacities of local institutions, to sustainably manage community socio-economic infrastructure/natural resources, and to promote food security, livelihoods and economic recovery in a gender-responsive manner
-	Establish/activate CMCs and other community structures (at least 50% women representation) and train them on basic management and technical aspects related to food security and livelihood interventions which is responsive of the needs of the most vulnerable, including women
-	Support the CMCs to set up cost recovery systems that ensure economic sustainability of the CMCs and the community-owned facilities 
-	Provide technical and financial support to relevant technical government institutions and civil society organizations to enhance their capacity to lead and facilitate local gender-responsive solutions to internal displacement.
